description: We are passionate high-school students from Pakistan united by our interest in space, astronomy, engineering, and technology. We bring diverse skills, ideas, and perspectives, and want to turn our curiosity into creative solutions for real-world challenges. We’re looking for teammates interested in space who can contribute skills in research, science, problem-solving, coding, design, and data analysis.
summary: We developed an interactive website portraying the story of the equipment sent to the moon and mars—that were later abandoned. The website addresses the significance of those equipments, how and why they were sent, and most importantly—why they were abandoned. This project introduces a wider perspective on how NASA equipment works and should not be forgotten- for the younger audience.
details: The project acts like an interactive memorial for all those abandoned objects sent as satellite or rovers to moon and mars. It is an immersive project, where the user can explore the website as an “astronaut” and go through the cards, created for the sole purpose of telling a story on the behalf of those equipments. It also has a memory retention portion, playing out as a quiz. This website is designed for the younger audience (8-14 year olds) that want to learn more about space engineering. It also continues the legacy of these objects, in a way that they arent forgotten. We used figma and canva for the UI design, html and css for the base code and freebuff ai coding agent for animations. Canva was mostly used for the pixel art theme, and fed into the project before deploying it. Our project is creative because it includes a participating certificate for the children who have explored the website. Moreover, it contains a creative manner of converting straightforward facts and figures into a fun interactive website. Our team kept in mind that our project was tailored towards beginners and the younger generation, therefore we did not bombard it with paragraphs full of complex statements and facts.
